metadata.name: RecipeBox Nightmare Recipe Import Test Set
metadata.purpose: Curated public URL set for stress-testing recipe import parsing, normalization, source preservation, and display behavior.
rules: URLs only; do not scrape or store recipe content in this fixture.
Do not bypass logins, paywalls, bot protections, or source access limits.
Use pages for importer QA only and respect each site's normal public access.
verification_notes: Curated from public recipe/video URLs and checked with status-only HTTP probes; no recipe bodies are stored here.
Some public browser-accessible sites return 403 to automated probes. Treat those as access-boundary tests and skip them if the importer receives a gate instead of recipe content.

must_pass_top_25.must_preserve: Long clean schema recipe with sauce, cheese, noodles, assembly, and bake stages.
Baking quantities and temperature from a clean schema page.
Brine versus roasting ingredients and timing.
Recipe card content while ignoring embedded video UI.
Source volume and gram weights for bread ingredients.
Tangzhong section separate from dough.
Repeated cake/frosting ingredients with correct direction refs.
Long-blog import with chill time and metric alternates.
Strawberry reduction, cake, and frosting components.
Dough, filling, and icing sections plus rise times.
Source-grounded banana tips as notes, not hallucinated additions.
Fermentation and bake ranges without collapsing them.
Metric weights, chocolate type/percentage, and brownie doneness cues.
Keep substitutions and toppings out of the required ingredient list.
Ignore cost metadata; preserve one-pot liquid/pasta ratios.
Metric/gas mark UK cake data.
Marinade/sauce stages and spice quantities.
Marinade ingredients and serving suggestions separated.
US and metric quantities without duplicate display.
Primary recipe versus variations.
Special-diet substitutions as source-grounded notes.
Marinade/sauce sections and Chinese pantry names.
Japanese pantry terms and egg/dashi quantities.
Ramen components and linked sub-recipe notes.
Large-batch dough, filling, icing, and yield.

nightmare_top_10.why: Tangzhong plus dough tests section parsing and source-provided metric handling.
Cake and frosting repeat ingredients; direction refs must point to correct section.
Dough, filling, icing, repeated butter/sugar, and timing ranges in one recipe.
Long fermentation windows and dough technique can bury the actual recipe structure.
Macaron weights, visual cues, resting, and filling expose brittle parsing quickly.
Metric-only brownie weights and chocolate percentages expose conversion and ingredient-name bugs.
International recipe with marinade/sauce sections and spice-heavy ingredient list.
Marinade, sauce, noodles, and wok technique stress section and ingredient-name preservation.
Ramen page can include broth, tare, toppings, noodles, and linked component recipes.
Large-batch cinnamon rolls combine dough, filling, icing, yield, and old-page formatting.

importer_preservation_notes: Prefer source-provided quantities over calculated conversions when both are present.
Keep raw ingredient lines for audit when available.
Do not collapse compound quantities such as '1/3 cup + 3 Tbsp'.
Keep vague amounts such as pinch, splash, scant, heaping, and to taste as written.
Do not import nutrition tables, related recipe modules, comments, ads, or video UI as recipe data.
When pages contain multiple components, preserve ingredient sections rather than flattening everything.
When pages contain multiple recipes or variations, import the primary recipe and store useful source-grounded variation notes separately.
For YouTube URLs, use transcript/description only; do not invent missing quantities from visual inference.
For paywall-boundary examples, skip if normal public access is not available.
